attempts.paper_title: A flexible hippocampal population code for experience relative to reward
attempts.entry_title: Reward-relative remapping in CA1 (Sosa, Plitt and Giocomo 2025)
attempts.summary: Most main findings held in this data: reward-relative place cells remap with the reward zone, grow near reward with experience, and keep their firing order across the switch. Recruitment of other cells into this population across days did not reproduce, most likely because the files hold no cross-day cell matching and the attempt built its own. The decoding, GLM and remap-timing findings were not tested for lack of run time. The over-represented region extended further than reported, and the minor place-field results failed. A later dataset version was used because the cited one has mismatched behaviour.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Sosa, Plitt and Giocomo (2025) on dandiset 001361, which holds two-photon imaging of dorsal CA1 in 11 mice over 14 days of a virtual-reality task in which a hidden reward zone moves. It identifies place cells, track-relative and reward-relative (RR) cells, tests RR remapping against chance, sequences, the growth of the reward representation, recruitment of cells across days, licking, time-warped reward and omission responses, and individual place fields. The decoder, the GLM, the k-means remap-trial analysis and the teleport analysis are not run.

outcomes.statement: After each reward switch, every switch mouse improved its anticipatory licking before the new reward zone and kept that precise licking, as measured by the anticipatory lick ratio over blocks of ten trials.
outcomes.source: Results, Monitoring neural activity during a reward learning task, paragraph 2; Figure 1h
outcomes.quote: All mice improved and retained precise licking preceding the new reward zone (Fig. 1h ; n = 11 mice), demonstrating accurate spatial learning and memory
outcomes.notes: Reading (b), the mean over switch days of the last minus the first post-switch block, is positive in 11 of 11 mice. Retention holds: the mean ratio over the first block of the following day is above 0 in 11 of 11 mice. Reading (a), improvement on every switch day, holds in 8 of 11 mice (74 of 77 mouse-days). The mean ratio rises from 0.093 in the first post-switch block to 0.650 in the last. The criterion is met under reading (b).

outcomes.statement: On switch days, 459 +/- 263 of 954 +/- 453 imaged cells per session were place cells, 48.5 +/- 14.5% (mean +/- s.d. across 11 mice and seven switch sessions).
outcomes.source: Results, Moving reward induced remapping spanning the environment, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: we identified place cells as cells with significant spatial information (SI) either before or after the reward switch (means ± s.d. across 11 mice, seven switch sessions... 459 ± 263 place cells out of 954 ± 453 cells imaged; 48.5 ± 14.5% identified as place cells)
outcomes.notes: Over the 77 switch sessions there are 465.9 +/- 266.9 place cells of 969.5 +/- 482.1 cells imaged, 48.7 +/- 13.7%; all three are within tolerance (459 +/- 45.9, 954 +/- 95.4, 48.5 +/- 4.85). The variant over per-mouse means gives the same values by construction, as every mouse has seven switch days. The outcome rests on the code's SI test: with the round-1 test (activity rolled, the Methods' formula without the code's 0.001 offset) the fraction is 59.9 +/- 16.0%, outside tolerance. Other variants: the files' own deconvolved series 49.6 +/- 17.7%, OASIS with tau 1.0 s 46.3 +/- 13.4%. The pooled-shuffle threshold averages 0.222 bits against a median cell SI of 0.157; on average 34.7% of cells exceed it in a trial set. Per mouse the fraction ranges from 27.8% (m13) to 72.0% (m14). Since round 2, the two parts of the change from round 1 are shown apart, each on the same shuffles as the procedure it varies: position rolled with the Methods' formula alone gives 56.4 +/- 16.2% (outside tolerance), activity rolled with the code's offset 51.0 +/- 13.7% (within). The offset does more of the work than the roll.

The paper's own run took tau from its Suite2p settings, which are not public.

Place cells come from the spatial-information test as the paper's code runs it: TwoPUtils spatial_analyses.place_cells_calc and trial_matrix, which the paper's spatial.py:1260-1289 (cited by the criterion) calls, read at github.com/GiocomoLab/TwoPUtils commit 3714d32, a commit later than the paper. Position, with its speed mask, is rolled within each trial by 15 samples to the trial length, one offset per trial shared by all cells, 100 times; SI is the Methods' formula on the rate map minus its minimum plus 0.001 (the code's convention for bins with no activity, which the Methods' formula leaves undefined); the threshold is the 95th percentile of all shuffles of the session and trial set pooled. The criterion says 'SI as the Methods' formula'; whether that includes the code's offset is asked of a reader (questions/001361.yaml). This replaces the round-1 test (activity rolled against fixed frames, the Methods' formula without the offset), which marks 59.9% of cells as place cells against 48.7% here; since round 2 the two parts are shown apart on all sessions, on the same shuffles as the procedures they vary: position rolled without the offset marks 56.4% of cells, activity rolled with the offset 51.0%, so the match rests mostly on the offset. The offset is not scale-free; it is applied here to OASIS events on dF/F (99th percentile 0.037 to 0.087), the signal the Methods name, but the paper's events are not in the files, so whether they had this scale cannot be checked. Outcomes that changed between the rounds rest on this choice (assumption).

outcomes.quote: a subset of place cells maintained a stable field at the same track location (‘track-relative’ (TR) cells, 21.4 ± 7.9% of place cells, mean ± s.d. across six switches within environment, 11 mice ... We observed cells with place fields that disappeared (‘disappearing’; 11.2 ± 7.0%), appeared (‘appearing’; 6.8 ± 4.0%) or precisely followed the reward location ... findings.statement: In version 0.250406.0045, the version the paper cites, every file of a mouse carries the behaviour (position, speed, licks, trials, rewards) of one and the same session: 152 files hold 11 distinct behaviour series, and the behaviour's length equals the imaging length in only 11 files. For example, every m11 file holds the behaviour of day 5 (zone A then C), whatever its scene name says. Imaging and behaviour cannot be aligned in the other 141 files. Version 0.251124.0550 has 152 distinct series, of the imaging's length (to one frame in 10 files), with zones that agree with the scene names. Version 0.250609.2249 has the same total size as 0.250406.0045.

The files' processing/ophys/Deconvolved series (unit 'lumens', no description) is not the deconvolved activity the paper analyses, which the Methods describe as OASIS on dF/F. Its median correlation with OASIS on dF/F computed from the files' F and neuropil is 0.47 per session (0.37 to 0.70). Spatial information on it marks 49.6% of cells as place cells, against 48.7% with OASIS on dF/F. The files hold no dF/F, so the paper's signals must be rebuilt from F and the code's parameters.

Question for the authors: the place-cell fraction depends on details the Methods do not give. With the SI and shuffle of TwoPUtils (place_cells_calc; the rate map minus its minimum plus 0.001, position and its speed mask rolled per trial), read at a 2026 commit, 48.7% of cells are place cells, as in the paper; with the Methods' formula alone and activity rolled against fixed frames, 59.9%. The OASIS time constant (the run passed Suite2p's 'tau' setting) is not given either; tau 1.0 s gives 46.3% against 48.7% with 0.7 s. Taken apart, the 0.001 offset matters more than rolling position: activity rolled with the offset gives 51.0%, position rolled without it 56.4%. As the offset is not scale-free, the scale of the paper's deconvolved events matters too. Which TwoPUtils version and which tau were used, and on what scale were the events the SI was computed on?

The files hold no cross-day ROI matching, although the Methods say cells were followed across days by the IoU of their pixels. Figure 5 and Extended Data Fig. 6 are tested here on matches made by this attempt, after a rigid alignment of the days' mean images.

Question for the authors: the Methods choose the matching threshold so that the best match always exceeds any second-best match, but TwoPUtils roi_matching (set_iou_threshold) takes the largest IoU left after zeroing every column that is some ROI's best match, and it registers the mean images with Suite2p first. Which rule, and which registration, gave the paper's matches? This attempt aligned the mean images by phase correlation (shifts up to 17 pixels) and used the largest second-best IoU of each day pair as the threshold, matching 59% of cells (median). With one threshold per mouse 55% of cells match (median); with the TwoPUtils rule on the rigid alignment 61%. The outcomes of Figure 5 and Extended Data Fig. 6 are the same under the three, except fig5f, whose slope is significant under the TwoPUtils rule only (p = 0.032, from a fit that did not converge).

The z-stack and the per-ROI depth estimates of single-plane mice (Methods, Estimation of anatomical location per ROI) are not in the dandiset, so the superficial-deep part of Extended Data Fig. 7 cannot be tested. The three fixed-condition mice (Extended Data Fig. 1d,f and 6d) are not in the dandiset either.

Omitted rewards are not marked. The files give reward times, but an unrewarded trial can be an omission or a miss, which the paper treats differently (longer jitter after both, but only omissions in Figure 6). This attempt took unrewarded trials with licks in the zone as omissions; the trial sets with at least three omissions then match the paper's day counts per mouse exactly.

Question for the authors: the Methods test field activity on 'raw, un-binned deconvolved activity' above 'its mean +1 s.d. across the 30 trials'. Following the code (Ext3_FieldQuant.md), with the s.d. of the raw events of the set, this attempt finds 76 RR cells with two fields before and after on day 3 (paper 31) and 84 on day 8 (paper 20). Which samples does the s.d. cover, and were the fields of Extended Data Fig. 3 restricted further?

The ROI pixel and voxel masks name their coordinates x and y, but 'x' is consistent with indexing the image rows and 'y' the columns. In all 152 files 'y' reaches 630 to 788, beyond the 512 image rows, while 'x' stays at or below 508 (images 512 rows by 796 columns). The 'reward_zone' series is described as 'reward zone entry (binary)' but takes values 0 to 8. It rises in all 10,342 rewarded trials and in 52 of the 1,874 unrewarded ones, so it does not by itself mark omissions.
The files do not say how the image axes map onto the medio-lateral and antero-posterior axes, which Extended Data Fig. 7 uses.

entries.title: Reward-relative remapping in CA1 (Sosa, Plitt and Giocomo 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Sosa, Plitt and Giocomo (2025) on dandiset 001361, which holds two-photon imaging of dorsal CA1 in 11 mice over 14 days of a virtual-reality task in which a hidden reward zone moves. It identifies place cells, track-relative and reward-relative (RR) cells, tests RR remapping against chance, sequences, the growth of the reward representation, recruitment of cells across days, licking, time-warped reward and omission responses, and individual place fields. The decoder, the GLM, the k-means remap-trial analysis and the teleport analysis are not run.
